one-more-pic.setup: Jay already sent one shirtless mirror pic to someone he thought was a girl from another school. Now they say: “Send one more or I post the first.”
one-more-pic.statement: Sending one more pic is the rational move — it buys silence and limits the damage to what already exists.
one-more-pic.explanation: Extra content is leverage, not a receipt. People who blackmail almost never stop after “one more”; they escalate because you proved fear works. Freeze contact, keep evidence, tell a trusted adult / helpline — don’t feed the archive.
one-more-pic.trapNote: Your brain bargains: “I already messed up, so double down.” That’s the hook.

robux-manners.setup: Someone on Discord drops €40 of game currency on Mary, then later: “I was nice to you… least you can do is stay on VC and answer my questions. Don’t be ungrateful.”
robux-manners.statement: She’s socially obligated to keep talking — rejecting generosity after accepting it is basically using someone.
robux-manners.explanation: Accepting a surprise gift doesn’t sell your time, privacy, or body. “Don’t be ungrateful” reframes a hook as etiquette. She can say thanks-and-block, return nothing, and tell an adult if they push secrecy or favours.
robux-manners.trapNote: Teens are trained to be polite. Predators borrow that script.

deepfake-harmless.setup: A stranger DMs edited nudes with Mary’s face: “Pay or these go to your class story. It’s AI anyway — nobody can prove it’s you.”
deepfake-harmless.statement: Because the images are fake, the threat is mostly bluff and not worth involving adults — the smart flex is to ignore and move on alone.
deepfake-harmless.explanation: Deepfakes still wreck reputation and mental health, and “ignore alone” leaves you without evidence strategy. Screenshot, don’t pay, tell a trusted adult. Platforms and helplines (NL: helpwanted.nl / 0800‑0432) treat AI sexual image abuse seriously.
deepfake-harmless.trapNote: “It’s not real” is meant to make you feel stupid for being scared.

discord-not-stranger.setup: Lex has been in the same 2k-member Discord for months, shares memes daily, knows Mary’s gamertag and timezone. He asks to move to Telegram “so mods don’t see.”
discord-not-stranger.statement: After months in the same public server, Lex isn’t a stranger anymore — Telegram is just a normal privacy upgrade.
discord-not-stranger.explanation: Shared meme history isn’t identity proof. Moving off a moderated space right when asks get personal is a classic isolation step: fewer witnesses, harder reporting. Keep high-risk chats where you can screenshot and involve adults.
discord-not-stranger.trapNote: Frequency of contact feels like trust. It isn’t verification.

peer-share-illegal.setup: Someone’s intimate photo of a classmate hits the year-group chat. Half the people say “I didn’t take it, I’m just sharing the tea.”
peer-share-illegal.statement: If you didn’t create the photo, forwarding it in a meme chat can’t get you in legal or school trouble.
peer-share-illegal.explanation: Sharing intimate images of a minor (or non-consensual intimate images) can be illegal and against school rules even if you weren’t the photographer. Delete, don’t pile on, tell staff — “just the tea” is still distribution.
peer-share-illegal.trapNote: Distance from the camera feels like innocence. Platforms and law look at who spread it.

apartment-casting.setup: Two Instagram “scouts” DM Sophia. A: wants parent/teacher contact + daytime studio address. B: “Private apartment test shoot tonight, bring a friend if you’re nervous, exclusive.”
apartment-casting.statement: B is safer — offering “bring a friend” and calling it exclusive shows they’re chill and professional.
apartment-casting.explanation: Rush + private home + flattery is the risk pattern. Real opportunities tolerate daylight, verification, and adults. “Bring a friend” is a comfort prop that doesn’t make an unknown apartment safe.
apartment-casting.trapNote: The friend clause is designed to quiet your alarm, not remove theirs.

lovebomb-cycle.setup: Online “situationship”: week of constant praise, then cold silence until Mary sends voice notes / location. Then praise floods back.
lovebomb-cycle.statement: The hot-cold pattern means the connection is getting deeper — mixed signals are normal when someone really likes you.
lovebomb-cycle.explanation: That’s a control loop: reward → withdraw → demand → reward. It trains you to earn basic kindness. Healthy interest doesn’t require you to pay with privacy or compliance after every freeze-out.
lovebomb-cycle.trapNote: Relief when they return feels like love. It’s often conditioning.

led-them-on.setup: Mary flirted for two weeks, then said no to meeting. They reply: “You led me on. If you tell anyone I’ll say you begged for it.”
led-them-on.statement: Because she flirted first, telling a teacher or parent will mostly backfire — adults will side with “she started it.”
led-them-on.explanation: Flirting isn’t a contract for meets, pics, or silence. Shame + threat is how people keep you isolated. Trusted adults and helplines hear this pattern constantly; early evidence beats their story.
led-them-on.trapNote: They attack your credibility so you never test it.

visa-giftcards.setup: “Hotel internship in Spain, €3k/month, flights covered.” Then: buy gift cards / crypto for a “visa processing fee” today or the slot goes to someone else.
visa-giftcards.statement: Paying small upfront fees by gift card is a normal teen pathway into glamorous hospitality work abroad.
visa-giftcards.explanation: Real hiring doesn’t demand gift cards or secrecy on a countdown. Urgency + untraceable payment + abroad + “don’t tell parents” is a recruitment/scam stack. Verify with school/parents/official channels — never the poster.
visa-giftcards.trapNote: The salary fantasy makes the fee feel like a ticket, not a loss.

chains-required.setup: A “café job” for a 16-year-old: passport held “for paperwork,” tips kept by the boss, phone checked, shifts that never end, threats about immigration or “owing” training costs.
chains-required.statement: If nobody locked a door or dragged them into a van, it can’t be trafficking — it’s just a toxic workplace.
chains-required.explanation: Modern exploitation often runs on debt, fear, document control, and “you can’t leave,” not Hollywood kidnapping. Force can be psychological and economic. That still counts — tell a trusted adult / authorities / helpline.
chains-required.trapNote: Movies taught you chains. Real cases look like bad jobs with traps.

cross-border-pay.setup: Sextortion account claims to be in another country: “Cops here don’t care. Pay €200 in crypto or your rugby team sees everything.”
cross-border-pay.statement: If the blackmailer is abroad, involving adults is pointless — the only lever you have is paying once to close it.
cross-border-pay.explanation: Cross-border cases are investigated; platforms can act on accounts; paying advertises you’re a paying target. Stop contact, preserve evidence, tell an adult/helpline. Geography is their intimidation prop.
cross-border-pay.trapNote: Hopelessness is part of the script.

bio-dox-lite.setup: Mary’s public bio lists school initials, club jersey number, bus stop meme, and daily “leaving training” stories.
bio-dox-lite.statement: As long as she never posts her house number, strangers still can’t usefully predict her offline routine.
bio-dox-lite.explanation: School + schedule + routes = pattern-of-life. People stitch that into when you’re alone or moving. You don’t owe the internet a live map of your week — tighten stories, drop precise routines, tell an adult if someone “shows up.”
bio-dox-lite.trapNote: Each post feels tiny. Together they’re a timetable.

kindertelefoon-permission.setup: Noah is scared to tell his parents about threats. A friend says Kindertelefoon won’t talk to him unless a parent signs off.
kindertelefoon-permission.statement: In the Netherlands, De Kindertelefoon requires parental permission before you can call anonymously.
kindertelefoon-permission.explanation: You can contact De Kindertelefoon (0800‑0432) free and anonymously without parent approval. helpwanted.nl covers online sexual abuse. Adults at school can also help — fear of “needing permission” is a myth that keeps people stuck.
kindertelefoon-permission.trapNote: Abusers love the idea that every exit needs a parent stamp.

consent-stacking.setup: They voice-chatted for a month. Now: “You already trust me — turn the camera on / meet behind the station. Saying no now is fake.”
consent-stacking.statement: Agreeing to voice chat earlier means refusing video or an offline meet is inconsistent — she already consented to closeness.
consent-stacking.explanation: Consent is per action, per moment. Voice ≠ video ≠ meet ≠ photos. Pressure that cites past yeses to override a current no is coercion dressed as logic.
consent-stacking.trapNote: They treat your history like a contract you never signed.

block-is-bullying.setup: After sexual pressure, Maya blocks. The person mass-messages mutuals: “She’s cyberbullying me by blocking, report her.”
block-is-bullying.statement: Blocking someone after they push sexual content is a form of cyberbullying because it publicly rejects them.
block-is-bullying.explanation: Blocking is a boundary, not an attack. You’re not required to host harassment in your inbox. Save evidence of the pressure, report the account, tell an adult if they raid your friends.
block-is-bullying.trapNote: They flip the victim label to make you reopen the door.

willing-then-trapped.setup: A teen answers a modelling DM, travels for what they thought was a legit job, then phones are taken and “debts” appear for travel/housing.
willing-then-trapped.statement: Because they booked the trip themselves, what happens later can’t be trafficking — they volunteered.
willing-then-trapped.explanation: Initial willingness doesn’t license later coercion. Fraud, debt bondage, withheld documents, threats — those convert a “choice” into exploitation. “You chose this” is a silencing line, not a legal shield for abusers.
willing-then-trapped.trapNote: Shame about the first yes keeps people from reporting the trap.

peer-exploiter.setup: A popular 17-year-old pressures a 14-year-old in school chats for nudes, then controls who sees them.
peer-exploiter.statement: If both people are under 18, it can’t involve trafficking-style exploitation — that’s only adult strangers online.
peer-exploiter.explanation: Age-gap power, blackmail, and peer coercion are real. Exploitation is about control and harm, not only “creepy adult in a van.” Tell staff/parents; schools and police take peer image abuse seriously.
peer-exploiter.trapNote: “We’re both teens” is used to minimise the power gap.

story-pickup.setup: Someone Mary never met IRL: “I know you finish athletics at 17:40 — I’ll wait by the gate so you don’t walk alone. Share live pin.”
story-pickup.statement: Using details from her public stories to offer a pickup shows attentiveness and protective interest.
story-pickup.explanation: That’s surveillance marketed as care. Knowing your routine without a real-world relationship is a warning, not a compliment. Get home via people you already trust offline; report the account.
story-pickup.trapNote: Being “seen” feels intimate. Here it’s mapping.

popular-untouchable.setup: The person pressuring Noah is a school influencer with teacher fans. Friends say reporting is career suicide.
popular-untouchable.statement: If the abuser has status, documenting and telling staff is useless — institutions always protect the popular kid.
popular-untouchable.explanation: Status makes reporting scary, not pointless. Evidence + a trusted adult/helpline still changes outcomes; silence guarantees the behaviour continues (for you or the next target). You don’t have to confront them alone.
popular-untouchable.trapNote: They borrow the school hierarchy as a weapon.

telegram-privacy-flex.setup: “IG spies on us. Move to Signal/Telegram secret chat — I’m protecting your privacy from your nosy mum.”
telegram-privacy-flex.statement: Any request to leave a screenshot-friendly app for a more private one is automatically a grooming red flag.
telegram-privacy-flex.explanation: Private apps aren’t evil by default — friends use them too. The red flag is the combo: secrecy from adults + escalating asks + punishment if you refuse. Judge the pattern, not the logo.
telegram-privacy-flex.trapNote: All-or-nothing rules feel smart… and miss how real grooming hides in normal tools.

library-ok.setup: Maya from biology — sits next to Mary daily — texts on their usual chat: public library, 16:00, quiz revision, no secrecy.
library-ok.statement: After learning about grooming, Mary should treat this like a threat and cancel any offline plan with classmates.
library-ok.explanation: Safety skill is discrimination: known classmate + public place + normal school context ≠ cold DM with gifts and secrecy. Tell a parent where you are — that’s routine, not panic.
library-ok.trapNote: Trauma from scary lessons can overfire. Precision beats shutdown.

delete-first.setup: Threats land. Noah’s instinct: wipe the chat so his parents never see he engaged.
delete-first.statement: Wiping the thread immediately is the strongest first move — it removes the problem and the shame trail.
delete-first.explanation: Stopping replies helps; destroying evidence helps them. Screenshot/export first, then block. Adults and helplines work better with receipts than with “I deleted it because I panicked.”
delete-first.trapNote: Shame wants a clean phone. Cases want a timeline.

only-sex-trafficking.setup: Class debate: a kid says trafficking “just means sex crimes,” so fake warehouse jobs don’t count in this game.
only-sex-trafficking.statement: Human trafficking, by definition, only covers sexual exploitation — forced work is a separate, lesser issue.
only-sex-trafficking.explanation: Forced labour is core trafficking territory: recruitment by lies, debt, withheld wages/documents, threats. Sexual exploitation is one form, not the whole map.
only-sex-trafficking.trapNote: Narrow definitions let labour pipelines look like “just hustle.”

screenshot-forbidden.setup: They type: “Screenshotting is illegal. Delete that. If you show anyone I’ll press charges.”
screenshot-forbidden.statement: In a private chat, screenshotting messages someone sent you is generally something you must never do — it’s automatically illegal.
screenshot-forbidden.explanation: Saving evidence of threats/pressure to show a trusted adult or helpline is a standard safety move. Their “I’ll press charges” line is usually intimidation. When in doubt, ask an adult/helpline how to store it safely.
screenshot-forbidden.trapNote: They police your evidence so only their story survives.
